abstract: The problem facing the UK is symptomatic of a long-running difficulty in workforce planning causing not just a shortage of skills, but a mismatch between the skills people have and the requirements of the jobs they currently occupy, says Jill Dann FBCS CITP. She looks at the value that SFIA 6 can add.

articleTitle: Cyber Forensics in a Post Stuxnet World
abstract: Computer forensics Masters student James Moos reports on the development of cyber security and forensics for industrial control systems in a post Stuxnet era.

Chris Reynolds FBCS follows up on Chris Yapp's Future Tech Blog post ‘The Limlit of Algorithms’ by looking at how that the explosive growth of the computer industry may have led to unconventional research on how people process information being abondoned.
Justin Richards MBCS spoke to Lee Randall, Head of Healthcare at RES Software, about the fact that there is ever more data to deal with and more that needs to be done with it.

Artificial pets have been shown to benefit people in similar ways to real pets. In addition to entertainment and social interaction they can also provide companionship. A paper in Interacting with Computers discusses this – and a formal way of measuring companionship benefit. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.
The following papers are from The Computer Journal, issue, Volume 58, 2015. The overviews are largely based on the abstracts. They are provided by Editor-in-Chief, Professor Fionn Murtagh.

Kevin Streater FBCS, BCS Learning & Development Specialist Group, argues that IT can help to solve global problems, but there is a real need for more critical thinking and problem solving skills from new IT trainees.
Professor Ursula Martin of the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford celebrates the 200th anniversary of the birth of Ada Lovelace with a look at her life and legacy.
CIO Tom Clark joined Leeds Building Society in 2013. He gives BCS an insight into empowering his teams to deliver an ambitious new change strategy.

We all know the stock answer to the question: what is your organisation’s greatest asset? Our pavlovian response is ‘our people’. But in the digital age we had better actually believe it, writes Adam Thilthorpe, Director for Professionalism at BCS.

There’s more than one type of identity crisis. Conventional identity theft is one thing but what of identity voyeurism? How much of us is in the shop window anyway? Are we in control? What are the risks? And where’s it heading?

Phillip Snalune, co-founder of the Codio coding and content platform, discusses why computational thinking is an important skill for school students to acquire, to enable them to contribute to the UK’s changing workforce…

articleTitle: Alchemy Bringing Members Volunteers and Staff Together
abstract: Paul Fletcher FBCS, Group Chief Executive, BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, joined the Institute in September 2014. He spoke to Brian Runciman MBCS about his background, his initial impressions of the organisation and more.
John is Managing Director of LHS Business Control, a member of BCS Council, a member of the Audit and Risk Committee and Chair of the Information Risk Management and Assurance SG.

Technology permeates all areas of our lives and we are increasingly reliant on it to perform the simplest of tasks – pay a bill, book a train, organise our day, entertain our children. But what about those who are more vulnerable? asks Jon Buttriss, CEO, BCS Learning & Development.
Andy Smith from the BCS Security Community of Expertise examines the security risks of data aggregation and mining.
David Bird MBCS CITP looks at the potential of 5G, and some of the security considerations that will need to be taken into account.
Paul Fletcher FBCS, Group CEO of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, explains the new strategy for the Institute and outlines its purpose.

The first article was published in Volume 58 Issue 8, August 2015. The second, third and fourth are from Issue 9, September 2015. These overviews are largely based on the abstracts. They are provided by Prof. Fionn Murtagh, who is Editor-in-Chief.

Data is everywhere. Some of this data is information we voluntarily give away through social media or other online tools, but data is also being generated as a by-product of us simply going about our day to day lives. This raises ethical questions, says John Quayle MBCS, a member of the BCS Ethics Specialist Group.

Louise Bennett, Chair of the BCS Security Community of Expertise, represented BCS on two panels at EuroDIG (European Dialogue on Internet Governance) on aspects of data protection and privacy – one related to identity and payments and the other to big data analytics and the internet of things. She reports on the event, entitled ‘Shaping the internet together’.
Kurt Roosen FBCS, Chair of BCS Council, emphasises the role and value of Council - and puts out a plea to get more members involved in this key part of the Institute.

Bill Jinks FBCS is an IBM Distinguished Engineer and for many years has been the Technical Adviser to the Wimbledon tennis championships, collecting and analysing data from matches. He spoke to Henry Tucker about his work.
When it comes to dealing with hacks such as the one Sony suffered, Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group says we should all learn from others mistakes.
Valory Batchellor and Neil Warburton from IBM take a look at the recent attack on Sony and ask what we can learn from it.

Are IT recruiters to blame? Are employers to blame? Do job seekers do enough? BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, hosted a dinner on 20 October 2015 to discuss the current state and future needs of recruitment and capability in IT. Under Chatham House rules, key recruiters and employers gave their views on what the problems might be. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

articleTitle: Women in IT Better Numbers in 2015?
abstract: If the answer is ‘Ahead of most of Europe, but behind Greece and Ireland’ what is the question? It’s: ‘How is the UK doing in terms of percentages of women working in IT?’ But is that enough cause for optimism? Brian Runciman MBCS reports.
It's not just top athletes who can make use of technology to help them improve, amateurs can do the same. Henry Tucker MBCS puts his running shoes on.
Steve Daniels FBCS CITP, Strategic Business Advisor for Cyber Security in CGI UK, looks at the best practices for secure cyber development now being adopted.
Gareth Baxendale FBCS CITP, Head of Technology, Clinical Research, Network National Institute for Health Research, looks at the ways to secure critical infrastructure.
David Bird asks, when it comes to the internet of things, is it a security car crash waiting to happen?

With today's smartphones, transferring money at a branch or ATM is quickly becoming a thing of the past. But how can you be sure that your money and personal information are secure when banking on your smartphone asks Alex Grant, Managing Director, Fraud Prevention, Barclays.

Do the ideas we have about ‘digital vision’ and the capability we actually need marry up? What is the real extent of the much-discussed IT skills shortage? Ben Rapp FBCS CITP gives his view from the ’unsexy underbelly of the tech industry’.

articleTitle: There’s Something in the Way you Walk
abstract: John Mitchell, Chair of the BCS Information Risk Management and Assurance Specialist Group, considers the current threat landscape and posits what may have to happen if the cyber defenders are to keep up with the cyber attackers.
A term used again and again where service levels cannot be agreed is ‘reasonable endeavours’. ITIL expert Simon Cook MBCS CITP asks what it means.
Mobility, convenience, work life balance, lean working practices – all support the view that we should enable and support mobile working, says Peter Taylor.

Jill Dann FBCS CITP, Director at Consultation Ltd, takes us on a whistle stop tour of BCSWomen Specialist Group's methods and tools.

articleTitle: Manifestos Making the UK the IT Place to Be
abstract: There will be a general election in 2015. In preparation many bodies have produced manifestos to try to influence government policy in the IT space. Are they asking for the right things? Brian Runciman MBCS reports on some of the manifestos and highlights some BCS reaction from a recent policy meeting.

articleTitle: Have you Ever Considered Retraining as a Computer Science Teacher?
abstract: If you relish the idea of inspiring people, fostering innovation and creativity and helping others to realise their potential then teaching computing is the career for you.

Paul D Jagger FBCS continues his assessment of information security from the perspective of one of its key principles, that of the availability of information. Here he continues looking at high availability solutions, this time in the form of disaster recovery solutions.

articleTitle: Digitally Enhanced Learning Facing Up to the Camera
abstract: Digitally enhanced learning is challenging many aspects of traditional education. Barry G. Blundell FBCS highlights some practical and ethical consequences of recording and streaming lectures.
Gareth Baxendale FBCS, Head of Technology, National Institute for Health Research, Clinical Research Network, University of Leeds, introduces himself and BCS's health informatics group, BCS Health.

‘We anticipate bunfights ahead,’ so said the Chair of NHS England's Accessible Information Standard (AIS) at the first advisory group meeting. Dr Howard Leicester MBCS reports on the current state of accessibility in the UK.

Claire Davenport, BCS Academy of Computing Education Outreach Manager, details how the academy is helping teachers deal with the change to school's curriculum with the addition of computing and also looks at the work of a Computing At School (CAS) hub.
Professor Max Bramer, Chair, BCS Specialist Group on Artificial Intelligence (SGAI), addresses some recent comments made by Stephen Hawking and Elon Musk on AI (artifi cial intelligence).

articleTitle: What Digital Leaders Want and Need
abstract: Everyone wants a larger budget, but when only 8 per cent of participants feel that their organisation has enough resources and more than 79 per cent indicate that they need enhanced IT skills among their existing workforce or additional IT staff, the digital leader has plenty on their plate for 2015. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

October 2013 saw the Ministry of Defence stand-up a new kind of Reserve unit, the Cyber Reserve. Our anonymous author is a serving officer in the Joint Cyber Unit (Reserve) and BCS member, and gives some insight into the way the new unit is being set up and asks: could you join?

articleTitle: Are there Invisible People in Your Organisation?
abstract: What do IBM, Microsoft, JustIT, The Royal Airforce, Waitrose and Allianz have in common? They are all recognising a group of IT workers who, until now, have not been heralded - their IT technicians. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

articleTitle: Creative Science Injecting Innovation into the IT Industry
abstract: Product innovation can be both an opportunity and a concern for IT companies. Those driving innovation can gain unprecedented market openings, while those trailing can risk disaster. Victor Callaghan, Professor of Computer Science at Essex University, explains.

The winning papers for The Computer Journal Wilkes Award for 2014 have been announced. Exceptionally, this year the prize has been awarded to two joint winners. These articles are now available free online, the extracts appear below.

There is mistrust in IT recruitment. With at least three perspectives to take into account - agency, employer and candidate - could it be contributing to the demise of the IT department? Brian Runciman MBCS looks at some of the issues.

abstract: Gareth Baxendale FBCS CITP and James Mucklow FBCS CITP take a look…

abstract: Brian Runciman MBCS speaks to Professor Ross Anderson, who won the 2015 Lovelace Medal and will be delivering the 2016 Lovelace Lecture. Professor Anderson, who is Professor of Security Engineering at University of Cambridge and a Fellow of Churchill College, has been awarded the medal in recognition of his many contributions to building security engineering into a discipline.

articleTitle: It’s All in the Mind You Know
abstract: Brian Runciman MBCS looks at the special issue of Interacting with Computers concerning brain and body monitoring systems.
Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Partner and Head of Eversheds' Tech, Media and Telecoms Sector, talks about a couple of hot topics relating to security in tech and media.
Identity is at the root of who we are as individuals when it comes to matters of trust, says Gareth Niblett, Chair of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group.
This is the first in a series of three articles by Paul Jagger FBCS CITP on the subject of information security from the perspective of one of its key principles: availability of information.

Professor Niloy J. Mitra has been awarded the BCS Roger Needham Award for 2015 sponsored by Microsoft Research Cambridge. The award has been made in recognition of his outstanding work in the area of computer graphics and 3D geometry.
There are around 12,000 women in BCS membership and 1,500 in the BCSWomen Group. Gillian Arnold, Chair of BCSWomen, says there are compelling reasons to join.
John Mitchell, Chair of the BCS Information Risk Management and Assurance Specialist Group, looks at the issues surrounding the collecting, storing and use of data.
Tony Proctor looks at the idea of an ‘internet passport.’

When it comes to cyber security, why do large companies do it so poorly, asks Rob Pritchard.
Terry Espiner, Client Director, UK Healthcare at Cisco, looks at the relationship between the IoE (internet of everything) and the transformation of the healthcare industry.

articleTitle: Convergence of Computing, Biogenetics and Cognitive Neuroscience
abstract: Charles Ross HonFBCS discusses the exciting possibilities of the convergence of mathematics, physics, computer science, philosophy and cognitive neuroscience, following the presentation in March 2015 to the Real Time Club and the Royal Institution by philosopher Daniel Dennett.

Andy Smith MSc FBCS CITP provides an update on the BCS Security Community of Expertise.
When it comes to security planning, John Mitchell says you can hope for the best, but you must also plan for the worst.

Nicholas Fernando, Head of Content, Filtered.com and Janet Cole, Chair, BCS Business Change Specialist Group, examine the expanding key skills of knowledge workers and ensuring effective learning support.

When it comes to choosing technology solutions, don’t shoot yourself in the foot says Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group.
When it comes to mobile security, John Mitchell will even risk his wife's ire in order to stay secure. It's that important.
While there were a number of prominent security incidents in 2014, there were undoubtedly more than those reported, says Nic Oatridge MBCS.

Steve Furber gave the BCS Lovelace Lecture 2015. Justin Richards interviewed him about his work, the importance of understanding the brain, ethics, professionalism in IT and more.
When it comes to dealing with cyber security, technologists must focus more on threats and controls and less on risk, says Neil Cordell.

abstract: In order to give something back to society at large, Paul Gartside and Graham Strachan from McAfee, part of Intel Security, have created an outreach programme that took them in directions they hadn’t planned.

Mike Freeman, Sales Director, Techne-Comm Ltd, discusses the importance of email archiving in the healthcare sector.
The BCS IT Awards judging day took place on 25 September. Brian Runciman MBCS enjoyed interviewing some of the entrants for the Apprentice of the Year.
Simon Marvell, partner at Acuity Risk Management, argues that the real and present threat of a cyber breach demands real-time risk management from organisations, both large and small.

Newcastle’s computing undergraduate degree can only claim to be 49 not out. However, we do believe that Newcastle can claim a significant contribution to the development of the curriculum, says John Lloyd FBCS.
Lee Wagstaff, Brand Development Manager, Thornton and Laurie, looks into why competition for IT contracts in the healthcare sector looks set to heat up.

Paul D Jagger FBCS CITP a Court Liveryman of The Worshipful Company of Information Technologists explores the role of the Company, its links with charity, education, industry and fellowship, the armed forces and the City of London's government.

When Henry Tucker went to CES2014 one of the things he was most impressed by were Audi's computercontrolled cars. You could park them simply by pressing a button on your smartphone. They could also takethe controls in slow moving traffic, but because of legislation they couldn't do more than that.

As the world of cyber evolves, we need to drive innovation which moves past the conventional IT world and the wider world of mobile devices and apps, to consider where else we need to innovate to ensure we keep safe wherever and however we connect, says Gareth Niblett, Chair of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group.

articleTitle: Data Protection Does it Apply to Start-Ups?
abstract: In the pressure to get a new product, software or service to market, security and privacy can often be overlooked. With this in mind, Dawn James MBCS, BCS Entrepreneurs Specialist Group, asks if the EU’s new General Data Protection Regulations apply to start-ups and entrepreneurs.

Without getting too tabloidy, Volume 27 Issue 4 of Interacting with Computers is looking at the emotion that played a key role in Philip K Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep - empathy. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

abstract: Julian Fletcher MBCS, E-learning Business Analyst and Director of Fletcher Business Analysis Services, asks: what would the ideal IT recruitment agency look like?

It's 50 years since the first students started studying for degrees in computer science. To commemorate this Professor Roy Newton FBCS and colleagues look back over half a century of computer science.

Let me tell you a semi-religious joke, always a bit of a risk I know!A leading technologist passed away peacefully in his sleep. On arrival at the electronic Pearly Gates in technology heaven he asked the virtual Peter for a brief orientation tour if he was to be granted entry - Peter was happy to confirm both. During the orientation tour, the technologist saw many heavenly technical sights - people just thinking and innovating, people collaborating at all levels, a real cloud instead of a virtual one and so on. Eventually they got to a closed-off area that had very high walls, behind which could be heard many voices, mainly male with lots of shouting and arguing. It was a very dark and closed area. ‘Who is in there?’ asked the technologist.‘Ah,’ said virtual Peter, ‘they are the CIOs, they think they are the only people here.’

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Partner and Head of Technology, Media and Telecoms Sector; Edward Norris, Commercial Associate; and Rebecca Sherry, Associate in the Privacy and Information Law Group, all of Eversheds LLP, look at some of the legal obligations which flow following a breach of IT security.

Does your IT team need to change to fulfil the requirements of your business? IT costs are increasing as a percentage of revenue and operation expenses and, at a time when many organisations see themselves as technology companies, IT costs are set to further increase. Louise McCarthy, IT Commercial Services and Performance Management Director at Specsavers, looks at the benefits of commercialising the IT department.

As we have all seen during the recent general election campaign the NHS remains a British institution which stimulates passionate debate irrespective of party politics. The challenge of providing universal healthcare free at the point of delivery is increasing as people live longer and expect more from the service.Dr Paul Mukherjee, Head of Services and Solutions, UST Global, reports.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Commercial Partner and TMT Sector Head, and Ben McLeod, Commercial Solicitor, both of Eversheds LLP, discuss the recent toughening of cybercrime legislation in the UK through the passing of the Serious Crime Act 2015 (the act) and examine the ways in which the Act will assist the government in achieving the objectives set out in the National Cyber Security Strategy.

articleTitle: So, What is the Future of the IT Team
abstract: This has been the first time ITNOW has run a feature from a guest editor, writes Brian Runciman MBCS. The issues raised are interesting, not only from an employer’s perspective, but all those working in the IT industry. That’s 1.18 million people for whom these issues are personal - about you, your current career and your future career in IT. Why not get involved in the follow-up?
Maria Kutar, Marie Griffiths and Gordon Fletcher look at how we can secure the increasing problem of multiple digital identities.

articleTitle: Cloud With a Chance of Regulation
abstract: The EU's regulatory planning for cloud computing and data protection is an expanding domain worthy of everyone's attention. Whether you are pro-EU regulation, or anti, the European Commission is addressing vital solutions to key issues so says Stephen Meachem, a barrister and solicitor with the Law Tribe and a member of the BCS Law Specialist Group.
